children: EU rules force Alphabet's GOOG to anonymize shared search data starting Jan 2027 and to enable third‑party AI assistants to access Google features like Gemini under new Android changes.
GOOG sued at the EU General Court over proposed rules forcing data sharing and wider Android access for rival AI tools, arguing the search-data rules lack safeguards and fail to secure user consent.
GOOG traded lower amid EU regulatory escalation, slipping about 0.8% intraday to near $336.40, later around $337.83, as markets reacted to the dispute and Google’s appeal.
GOOG joined the White House AI Safety Accord, committing to internal monitoring, independent external audits, a board-level oversight committee, and ongoing teams to ensure monitoring systems work.
GOOG is removing Google Assistant from phones and tablets across the U.S. and Europe; mobile users will see Gemini replace Assistant as the default on affected devices.
GOOG backed a four-tier AI oversight plan: internal controls, internal review teams, outside auditors, and independent board review; no specific audit firms or methods were mandated.
Alphabet Inc. Class C (GOOG) cited as an early customer for SpaceX’s growing AI compute capacity, projected to rise from 2.1 GW in 2026 to about 6 GW by end‑2027.
